title: Hypersingular Riesz-energy constants on surfaces from triangular-lattice universal optimality
seo_title: Riesz-energy constants on surfaces | Alec Kriebel
meta_description: An attributed consequence of triangular-lattice universal optimality: exact leading Riesz-energy constants on smooth surfaces for each fixed s > 2.
abstract: We deduce the exact two-dimensional hypersingular minimal Riesz-energy constant for every real s>2 from OpenAI's recently released triangular-lattice universal-optimality theorem. The constant is the Epstein sum of the covolume-one triangular lattice. An explicit gap-periodization argument relates the finite square problem to the source theorem's centered-disk lower energy, with an inter-box error of order N^(1−s/2) for each fixed gap parameter. A lattice crop gives the matching upper bound. The corrected Hardin–Saff universality theorem then gives the ordered-pair leading asymptotic on every smooth compact embedded surface of positive area, including surfaces with smooth boundary, for ambient Euclidean distance. This resolves the two-dimensional s>2 case of the explicit lattice-constant conjecture recorded by Brauchart, Hardin and Saff. The universal-optimality breakthrough, finite-to-infinite reduction and manifold theorem are inherited results; this note gives a self-contained account of the known passage and records its planar surface consequence.
